nodes.name: Dipterocarp trees
nodes.desc: Dipterocarps such as Dipterocarpus, Shorea and Dryobalanops dominate the lowland forest here and form its tall canopy.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Fruiting figs and geocarpic figs grow widely in the park, and birds feed on them.

nodes.name: Segera
nodes.desc: A rainforest tree well recorded near the park. GloBI has a record of the Asian palm civet eating its fruit.

nodes.name: Understorey palms
nodes.desc: Small palms of the shady forest floor; the park also has abundant rattan, gingers and ferns beneath the canopy.

nodes.name: Bornean bearded pig
nodes.desc: A forest pig that roots through the leaf litter for fallen fruit, seeds and invertebrates.

nodes.name: Long-tailed macaque
nodes.desc: An adaptable monkey that eats fruit, seeds and small animals and is recorded in the park area.

nodes.name: Eastern grey gibbon
nodes.desc: Wikipedia calls it the best-known arboreal mammal of the park, living mostly in the canopy. Gibbons mainly eat fruit.

nodes.name: Prevost's squirrel
nodes.desc: A colourful tree squirrel that eats fruit, seeds and some insects. It is one of the most recorded mammals near the park.

nodes.name: Rhinoceros hornbill
nodes.desc: A large forest bird, well recorded here. Mostly fruit, but it also takes insects, small reptiles and other small animals.

nodes.name: Giant honey bee
nodes.desc: A wild bee that hangs open combs from high branches and feeds on flower nectar. It is one of the best-recorded insects near the park.

nodes.name: Prickly stick insect
nodes.desc: A large leaf-eating stick insect of Bornean forests, recorded repeatedly near the park.

nodes.name: Asian palm civet
nodes.desc: A night-active omnivore that eats fruit and small animals. GloBI records it eating Aglaia fruit near the park.

nodes.name: Green crested lizard
nodes.desc: A slender tree lizard that hunts insects among the foliage and is in turn eaten by birds and snakes.

nodes.name: Striped bronzeback
nodes.desc: A slender tree snake. GloBI records it eating the common tree frog and a skink.

nodes.name: Common tree frog
nodes.desc: A tree frog that catches insects at night; GloBI records it as prey of the striped bronzeback.

nodes.name: Blue-throated bee-eater
nodes.desc: A bird that catches flying insects in the air. GloBI records it eating the giant honey bee near the park.

nodes.name: Sunda clouded leopard
nodes.desc: The largest carnivore on Borneo. Reported prey include deer, bearded pigs and primates.

nodes.name: Reticulated python
nodes.desc: An ambush hunter that squeezes its prey. Small ones eat rodents, bigger ones take civets and primates.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Equatorial sun feeds both the tall canopy and the plants that survive in the shade below.

nodes.name: Year-round rain
nodes.desc: Heavy rain keeps the lowland rainforest wet, with rivers such as the Temburong and Belalong running through it.

nodes.name: Forest soil & nutrients
nodes.desc: Leaf litter and dead wood return nutrients to the soil, where tree roots take them up again.

nodes.name: Termites, fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses and release nutrients to the soil.
